title: Research: Eisenstein E8 decoder copy floor 23 via submatrix-minrank certificates (past the clique-method limit; no κ claim)
body:
## Result

**Scoped lower bound; no supplier, no κ change, selected record untouched.**

In the abstract Eisenstein E8 scalar binary decoder model of `research/eisenstein-clique-copy-bound` (Jonathan Lam, PR798), every fitting decomposition costs **at least 23** pairing-rank units. PR798 proved 22 and showed that no weighting of cliques can prove more. Its PROOF.md says a stronger bound needs a new ingredient. This package supplies one: rank bounds on non-clique principal submatrices.

- **Lemma 1.** Zero-cost totals touch only free orthogonal entries, so they can be dropped.
- **Lemma 2.** Let `m(S)` be the least F2 rank of `B[S,S]` over fitting `B`. Then `m(S)` is at most the number of positive-cost totals meeting `S` on both sides. Weights satisfying `sum_S λ_S [F meets S][G meets S] <= c(F,G)` on every flat pair with `c >= 1` prove `C >= sum λ_S m(S)`. Cliques are PR798's special case. Asymmetric row and column sets add nothing.
- **New sets.** Take `S_uw = N[u] ∩ N[w]`, where `u,w` are nonorthogonal; there are 540 such sets of 20 lines each. Each splits as `I_2 ⊕ core`, with an 18-line core of clique number 5. An exhaustive normalized search (`U[Q]=V[Q]=[I_5|0]`) excludes every fitting completion of rank ≤ 7, and a rank-8 completion exists, so `m(S_uw) = 10`. Under PR798's optimal clique dual these sets are priced at 9.5. Five pinned automorphisms generate a group transitive on all 540 nonorthogonal pairs, so the search runs once.
- **Certificate.** Use weights `184/6835` (singletons), `13/13670` (2,880 seven-cliques) and `7/20505` (`S_uw`). They satisfy all 296,321 positive-cost flat-pair inequalities exactly, with 601 tight. The objective is `30200/1367 ≈ 22.092`, so **C ≥ 23**.

**Consequences.** The abstract optimum moves from [22,40] to [23,40]. PR1794's necessary window for an Eisenstein supplier shrinks from C ≤ 31 to 23..31. PR798's conditional three-stage Dfc window shrinks from 22..26 to 23..26. Neither route is closed.

**How far the method goes (exploration, not replayed).** I enumerated all 858,299 hit-maximal sets `⋂_{a∈A} N[a]`; every set has the same price as one of them and no larger minrank. They fall into 78 (|A|, |S|, price) classes. SAT minranks on class representatives and the class-uniform LP give exactly 30200/1367 again, and only the `S_uw` class beats the clique dual. If those classes are automorphism orbits (not checked), principal-submatrix certificates top out at 23.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/eisenstein-submatrix-copy-floor/verify.py
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/eisenstein-submatrix-copy-floor
```

- `verify.py` is standard library only. It passed on CPython 3.10, 3.12 and 3.14 in 35–58 s. The registered 3.12 replay, `--check-only` and the 42 research tests also pass.
- There are five rejection controls: the clique rank 6/7 search sanity check, a non-automorphism, a non-transitive generator subset, an inflated `S_uw` weight, and cliques-only weights falling below 22.
- Independent cross-check (SAT, not shipped): the normalized rank-7 instance is UNSAT for every one of the core's 112 five-cliques.
- One OpenAI Codex read-only review found no soundness issue (Lemmas 1–3, search completeness, automorphism reduction, i ≤ j symmetry, rounding). Its two wording fixes are applied: the positive-cost pair count, and an explicit `m(P,Q)` definition with the method-limit statement kept conditional.
- Not done: proof assistant, independent human review, any physical or supplier reading beyond PR798's premises.

## Scope and credit

The model, premises and geometry are PR798's; the pinned `geometry.py` is imported unchanged. Whole K-lines, scalar binary totals and the fitting pattern are essential. Nonlinear messages and sub-line operations are not covered.

Chooser seed `8bcd09ea00ac64eec3911b4b0c15e635` (complex-mechanisms / complex-rank-shape-decoder), scope **changed**; the reason is in `TASK.json`. Base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167#discussioncomment-18926981

Credit: Jonathan Lam (@jonathanlam, PR798: model, geometry, clique certificate, method-limit theorem); Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (PR620 geometry); Douglas R. Colkitt (PR703) and Sagar Thakrar (PR738) for the weighted-clique method; Maximooch (PR1794) for the window screen; DreamingOfClouds for naming the target. New material is by Josie Elliston, prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code, with substantial AI assistance in search, proof and verifier. Apache-2.0.
